blindComparison: A stranger picks the reference title, and for `wide` — the frame that would be the store hero image — the reason is a single sentence: there is not one cast shadow anywhere on the plateau. Fifteen stone lanterns, two torii, a banner pole and a fence line stand on open ground under a low magic-hour sun, and every one of them meets the ground with a symmetric halo instead of a raking shadow. Tsushima's equivalent shot is *made* of those shadows — they are what tells you where the sun is, how late it is, and how big the ground is. Strip them and the props read as stickers laid on a texture. The measurement behind the eye: the open plateau cobble (box 1500,950 160x60, cropped and confirmed to be bare cobble with no prop in it) has R/B = 46.5/40.3 = 1.154, statistically the same as the *shadowed* flagstone in `torii` (1300,1055 140x45, R/B 45.9/39.0 = 1.177) and 42% cooler than `torii`'s lit flagstone (850,1110 140x45, R/B 68.0/41.5 = 1.639) — from the same run, the same build, the same sun. The `torii` frame proves the key light and the shadow cascades work. `wide` proves they are not reaching the surface that matters most.
notesOnApparatus: Apparatus held. Five frames, one run, 2532x1170, all judged at 1:1 via `tools/probe.mjs crop`. Two instruments were written for this pass and both were validated against probe.mjs to the digit before use: (a) a pixel->fraction wrapper, checked by running `probe.mjs stats shots/phone-hero-r18v1.png 0.520,0.850,0.045,0.045` and the wrapper on 1317,995,114,53 and getting the identical line {meanRGB:[7.6,7,6.9], saturation:0.343, p50:4.6, detail:3.32}; (b) a contrast-stretch encoder, checked by round-tripping the same box at lo=0/hi=255 and md5-matching probe.mjs's own crop byte for byte (108ec1f6c773b6b5ea3f8ec2e6032005). The recurring 3-channel/4-byte-stride bug was specifically excluded by (a): the selfcheck path re-derives meanRGB from img.channels and agrees exactly. `detail` (mean |Laplacian|) is used only for fine-texture claims and never for structure claims. Every probe box quoted below was cropped and looked at before it was quoted; four candidate boxes were discarded during that check because they contained a lantern finial (torii 520,640), a lantern base (hero 1560,1000), or a sky sliver (wide 1300,250) — the replacements are named in the findings. On the refined binding rule for light evidence: the sun-arc profile used for the god-ray call is at r=420 px about the disc at (1526,516), angles 154 deg to 206 deg, sampling x in [1106,1162] — cropped (1080,270 130x450) and confirmed to be unbroken sky, with the near torii upright's screen footprint x in [1165,1270] lying strictly between every sample and the disc. It therefore excludes all geometry that could be mistaken for light while containing a genuine visibility step (the post's edge at x=1165 is 3 px outside the sampled span). It is not a clean-sky sector chosen for cleanliness; it is the sector the post is supposed to be shadowing.
plazaVoidVerdict: STILL PRESENT, and effectively unchanged to the eye. The argument-order fix moved the primary void (box 1317,995 114x53, cropped and confirmed to contain the amoeba-shaped patch left of the near lantern) from p50 3.1 / detail 2.95 to p50 4.6 / detail 3.32, and the second void (2020,1050 100x50) from p50 4.1 to p50 5.1. Both still read p1 = 0. Against the clean adjacent ground reference (1150,1090 114x53, cropped and confirmed to be warm-lit flagstone with no prop in it) at p50 31.1, the void is still 6.8x darker; in linear terms code 4.6 is ~0.0015 against ~0.0125, a factor of 8.3. A gain of 1.5 code values at the bottom of the sRGB toe is roughly 0.0005 linear and is below any viewing threshold — it is not a subtle improvement, it is not an improvement. They still read unambiguously as holes in the ground: a razor boundary with no penumbra, the flagstone crazing stopping dead at the edge, and no caster above them. What the fix *did* prove is that the surface is not empty: stretching the void interior 0->24 (crop 1240,950 400x200) reveals a mottled olive-green lobed clump texture inside it, so this is a foliage ground card carrying full albedo detail and receiving essentially no light — the light is being removed, not the reflectance. The prediction of ~49.2 / ~10.55 was 10.7x the delivered p50; whatever was fixed was real but was not the term that dominates. Two further voids are visible at 1020,1120 and along the bottom edge of the frame, and the same defect family appears in `valley` as blue-black blotches in the dirt mound (1450,1050 260x90).
godRayVerdict: NO. There are no volumetric shafts in either frame, and this is not a question of strength — it is a question of kind. What the pass delivers is an isotropic radial halo around the disc. `sun`: stretching the sky 150->235 over crop (700,250 1300x650) shows a perfectly circular falloff with clouds and nothing else — no wedge, no beam, no dark band behind the near torii upright, no structure keyed to any silhouette in the frame. The arc measurement is the same statement as a number: along r=420 px about the disc at (1526,516), the fifteen samples from 154 deg to 206 deg — every one of them in unbroken sky, every one of them with the near upright's footprint x in [1165,1270] interposed between it and the disc — read 211.9, 213.3, 215.4, 215.4, 215.7, 216.7, 218.5, 219.8, 220.7, 221.4, 221.6, 221.7, 222.4, 222.4, 213.7. Total spread 10.5 codes, no ordering, no correlation with the post's edges. Sky that is fully occluded from the sun is indistinguishable from sky that is not. `valley`: the frame is the contract's own example — bamboo backlit by a low sun through mist, ARCHITECTURE 5 non-negotiable #4 — and stretching the background 175->215 (crop 900,350 1200x400) returns a purely vertical gradient with zero angular structure. Not one shaft crosses a culm. This is the frame in the set where shafts would do the most work and there are none. Judged as a frame and not as an argument: the single feature that most separates Tsushima's and Sekiro's bamboo and torii approaches from this build is absent, in the two shots chosen to show it.
gateVerdict: `valley` black gate (p0.1 = 18-19 against < 15, 0.051% below code 16): NOT a real tonal fault as posed, but it is pointing at one. Mapping every pixel below 16 (2x block mask over the full frame) returns 0.14% of blocks, all of them isolated single-pixel aliasing speckle in the right-hand grass — no coherent dark region anywhere. The frame is a fully backlit mist scene: physically it *should* have no deep blacks, and demanding them would mean lifting the mist or breaking the backlight. So the gate as written should not be enforced on this pose. But the reason it fires is not only the mist. The deepest interior of the bamboo thicket, behind three or four layers of leaf at 5-15 m (1500,700 200x150), measures p1 39.9 — the same floor as a near culm in the immediate foreground (320,350 90x260, p1 39.5). In a real grove the gaps behind stacked leaves go near black; here leaf-on-leaf stacking produces no darkening at all, so the frame has no luminance depth and everything sits in one band. In the luma-only view the near culms are barely separable from the fog behind them. The honest reading of the gate failure is 'the near foliage has no self-occlusion', not 'the composition has no blacks'. Retire the numeric gate for this pose; keep the self-occlusion problem (it is finding 4). `sun` pctAbove240 (2.635% measured here, against a 0.5% guard): ACCEPTABLE, and the guard is wrong for this framing. Mapping every pixel above 240 shows them to be exactly four things — the sun disc and its immediate halo, the two paper lanterns, and the specular glitter path where the low sun hits the wet flagstone (crop 900,850 1200x320). That specular path is the best single element in the entire set. A shot pointed into a low sun that does not blow 2-3% of its pixels is a shot with a broken exposure. A 0.5% ceiling applied to an into-the-sun framing is a guard that would force the frame to be worse; it should be raised to ~4% for this pose or scoped to exclude the disc and emissives.
overallStanding: Honest read, both directions. This build is not close to Ghost of Tsushima or Sekiro, and it is also not a toy. Three things in this set would survive a 1:1 crop in a shipped title: the near bamboo in `valley` (crop 240,250 500x500 — cylindrical falloff on the culms, real node rings, leaves with veining, edge variation and genuine translucency), the wet-stone specular path in `sun` (crop 900,850 1200x320), and the shrine architecture in `torii` (crop 500,550 1300x470 — shoji lattice, roof tile courses, vermilion lacquer measuring correctly, a shimenawa that reads as rope). The sky is a real sky with chroma structure and believable cloud form. That is a genuinely high floor, and none of it is what is holding the build back. What is holding it back is that the lighting is not finished, and lighting is the top of the critic's priority list precisely because everything below it inherits the failure. Concretely: the establishing shot has no cast shadows and no true blacks or clean highlights (whole frame in [11,220], 95% of pixels inside [18,168], 0.005% above 240); the hero shot has lightless holes in its foreground; the two shots the contract nominates for god rays have none; and the shot named 'valley' contains no valley. Any one of those is a store-screenshot disqualifier on its own. Where it actually stands: the best crops are around 75-80 against the bar, the establishing shot is below 45, and because the establishing shot is the one a stranger sees first, the set as a whole reads 58. The three things that would move it most, in order: (1) Get the key light and the shadow cascades onto the `wide` plateau. This is worth more than every other item combined — it converts the weakest frame into the strongest composition in the set, and it is the only fix that improves silhouette, tonal range, palette temperature and material response simultaneously. (2) Kill the near-black ground cards. Three separate frames have patches of world that receive no light, and a hole in the ground is the one defect a viewer cannot rationalise. (3) Rebuild the mid-distance foliage LOD. The rectangular block mosaic that stands in for the forest ring appears in four of five frames, is more desaturated (0.093) than the mountain it occludes (0.131), and is the reason the middle distance reads as a matte painting. God rays are fourth, not third — they are a contract item and they are absent, but a frame with correct shadows and no shafts still reads as a real place, whereas a frame with shafts and no shadows does not. One structural note that no finding covers: there is no character in any of the five frames. This is a third-person sword-action game and the review set contains no player, no enemy, no blade, no trail, no rim light — which means non-negotiable features 6, 8 and 10 have never been reviewed at all. Whatever the next milestone is, the capture set needs a combat framing before this build can be judged as a game rather than as an environment.

findings.problem: At least four hard-edged, near-lightless voids lie in the lit flagstone of the near-foreground plaza. The largest sits immediately left of the focal stone lantern (box 1317,995 114x53, cropped and confirmed): amoeba/keyhole outline, razor boundary, no penumbra, no caster above it, and the flagstone crazing stops dead at its edge. It measures p50 4.6 / p1 0 / meanRGB [7.6,7.0,6.9] against clean adjacent lit flagstone at 1150,1090 114x53 (cropped and confirmed to contain ground only) at p50 31.1 / meanRGB [46.2,30.8,26.0] — 6.8x darker in code, 8.3x darker in linear. A second void at 2020,1050 100x50 reads p50 5.1, a third at 1020,1120, a fourth clipped by the bottom edge. This is not a shadow: a cast shadow in this same frame's plaza sits at p50 28-36 with a soft edge and the same texture running through it. The surface is not empty either — stretching the interior 0->24 (crop 1240,950 400x200) shows a mottled olive lobed clump texture at full albedo detail. Light is being removed from a foliage ground card, not reflectance. Last round's change moved this box from p50 3.1 to 4.6 and from detail 2.95 to 3.32, which is invisible.
findings.why: A patch of ground that receives no light reads as a hole punched through the world. It is the one class of defect a player cannot rationalise as 'dark' — it sits in the brightest, sharpest, most foveated part of the frame, adjacent to the shot's focal prop, and it tells the viewer the renderer is broken. No shipped title ships a store screenshot with a black hole in the foreground.
findings.fix: The ground clump cards in the near plaza must receive the same direct light as the flagstone they lie on. Target: box 1317,995 114x53 reaches p50 >= 25 and detail >= 6.0, and box 2020,1050 100x50 reaches p50 >= 22. Guard: the clean adjacent-ground box 1150,1090 114x53 must hold p50 31.1 +/- 3 and meanRGB R/B 1.78 +/- 0.15, so the fix is shown to raise the cards rather than flatten the plaza. Satisfiability check: the two target boxes total 11,042 px = 0.37% of the 2,962,440-px frame, and every pixel in them currently sits below the frame median (76), so raising them to 22-25 leaves them still below the median and cannot move whole-frame p50 by a single code — the target and the guard are on disjoint boxes and are mutually satisfiable with margin. Do not attempt this by lifting the global shadow floor: that was the round-16 regression and it would fail the p1=0 blacks in this same frame.
findings.hypothesis: The +1.5-code result against a ~46-code prediction suggests the winding fix corrected a term that is not the dominant one for these cards — e.g. the card is now lit correctly by the key but is still multiplied by a near-zero AO/occlusion or vertex-colour term, or the prediction's reference frame differed in more than foliage presence. Disprove before acting: ablate each multiplicative term on this card class one at a time and report which one, removed alone, moves box 1317,995 p50 above 20.

findings.problem: There are no volumetric light shafts in either frame — not weak ones, none. ARCHITECTURE 5 non-negotiable #4 names 'volumetric god rays through the torii and bamboo' and both framings exist to show it. `sun`: the sky under a 150->235 stretch (crop 700,250 1300x650) is a perfectly circular halo about the disc with cloud form and no angular structure whatever. Quantified on sky that is provably occluded from the sun: at r=420 px about the disc at (1526,516), the fifteen samples spanning 154-206 deg all lie at x in [1106,1162] — cropped (1080,270 130x450) and confirmed unbroken sky — with the near torii upright's footprint x in [1165,1270] interposed between every sample and the disc. They read 211.9 to 222.4, a 10.5-code spread with no wedge, no ordering, and no correlation with the post's edges. Fully-occluded sky is indistinguishable from unoccluded sky. `valley`: stretching the background 175->215 (crop 900,350 1200x400) returns a purely vertical gradient; not one shaft crosses a culm, in a frame that is backlit bamboo through mist.
findings.why: Low-sun shafts through a torii and through bamboo are the single most recognisable image in both reference titles. Without them the sun is a bright circle pasted on a sky rather than a light source occupying the same air as the geometry, and the frame loses all sense of atmosphere having volume. A radial blur around the disc is a glow filter, and it reads as one.
findings.fix: Produce shafts as shadow-sampled volumetric fog rather than as a screen-space radial gather. Target, checkable on the unstretched native frame: in `sun`, at least three distinct shafts visible at 1:1 in crop 700,250 1300x650, each >= 200 px long, anchored on a real silhouette edge (upright, kasagi, shide or treeline), and >= 12 codes brighter or darker than the sky immediately beside it at the same radius from (1526,516); and in `valley`, at least two shafts crossing the near culms in crop 300,60 1500x700. Guard: `sun` whole-frame p50 holds 111 +/- 5 and pctAbove240 stays <= 3.5% (currently 2.635%); the sky arc's mean at r=420, 154-206 deg holds 218 +/- 8 so the effect is differential and not a global brightening. Satisfiability check: three shafts at 200x30 px is ~18,000 px = 0.61% of frame, so a 12-code move on them shifts whole-frame p50 by 0 codes and pctAbove240 by at most 0.6 points — target and guard are mutually satisfiable, and 12 codes clears the current 10.5-code total sector spread so a pass would be unambiguous. Routing note, stated as reasoning and not as a claim about existing code: round 18's own arithmetic put the screen-space pass's ceiling at 4.43 codes against a 10.0 target, which is below any target that would be visible; ARCHITECTURE 8 assigns volumetric fog to this file, so that is where a mechanism with the necessary headroom lives.
findings.hypothesis: The measured behaviour — occluded sky at the same value as unoccluded sky — is what a pass that adds a common-mode term rather than a differential one would produce, which is also what round 15 concluded from the other side ('it smears a 10%-coverage emitter across 99.9% of the frame'). Do not act on this without first ablating: set the pass's contribution to zero and confirm the r=420 sky arc moves by more than its own 10.5-code spread. If it does not, the pass is not drawing those pixels at all and no parameter in it can matter.

findings.problem: The plateau — the lower 55% of the establishing shot — has no key light and nothing standing on it casts a shadow. Under an 80-code stretch (crop 500,720 1600x450) roughly fifteen stone lanterns, two torii, a banner pole and two fence runs all meet the ground with a symmetric warm halo and zero directional occlusion. At the ~13 deg sun elevation this build runs, a 3 m lantern owes a 13 m shadow and the torii a 21 m one; there is not one. The colour says the same thing: open cobble at 1500,950 160x60 (cropped and confirmed free of props) reads meanRGB [46.5,39.5,40.3], R/B = 1.154, which matches the *shadowed* flagstone in `torii` at 1300,1055 140x45 (R/B 1.177) and is 42% cooler than `torii`'s lit flagstone at 850,1110 140x45 (R/B 1.639). The entire visible plateau behaves like a surface in shadow, out to several hundred metres, where no occluder could reach. The `torii` frame from the same run has an obvious diagonal cast-shadow band with a warm/cool split across it (crop 700,1000 1200x170), so the key light and the cascades demonstrably work somewhere in this build.
findings.why: This is the frame that establishes the place, and shadows are how a viewer reads ground scale, time of day and the direction of the light. Without them the props sit on the texture rather than in the world, the plateau reads as one flat plane at one depth, and the whole shot goes to the grey mid-band the priority list names first. It is the single largest gap between this set and a Tsushima establishing shot.
findings.fix: The visible plateau in `wide` must receive the same key light and cast-shadow treatment the `torii` plaza already does. Target: (a) open-cobble box 1500,950 160x60 reaches R/B >= 1.40 (midway between the measured shadowed 1.177 and lit 1.639, deliberately conservative); (b) at least one cast shadow is legible at 1:1 in crop 700,780 1200x390, with a lit box and an adjacent in-shadow box on the same cobble giving a p50 ratio >= 1.8 (the `torii` pair gives 50.6/36.3 = 1.39 in code and the round-8 ablation measured 2.16 on the same surface, so 1.8 is inside demonstrated range). Guard: whole-frame p50 must stay <= 105 (currently 90) and pctAbove240 <= 1.0% (currently 0.005%). Satisfiability check: the cobble class sits at p50 39.5-54.7, i.e. below the frame median of 90; warming and shadowing it moves those pixels within the lower half of the histogram, so the frame median can only drift a few codes upward — the 105 ceiling leaves 15 codes of headroom against a target that needs none of it. This finding and finding 8 (tonal range) must land in the same round: adding key light is what creates both the deeper shadows and the cleaner highlights finding 8 asks for, and doing 8 alone by grading would erase the evidence for 3.
findings.hypothesis: Two candidates, both unproven and both cheap to kill before any code changes. (i) The plateau surface visible in `wide` is a different mesh or LOD from the flagstone in `torii` and is not in the shadow receiver set. Test: render `wide` and `torii` with the shadow term forced off and diff each against its own baseline — if `wide`'s ground is byte-identical and `torii`'s is not, the receiver set is the answer and nothing about cascade coverage matters. (ii) The `wide` eye sits far enough out that the visible plateau falls beyond the last cascade. Test: read back the cascade split distances and the ground distance range for this pose before touching anything. Note the standing record: 'no cast shadow on the plaza' has been filed and disproved three times for `hero` and `torii`, so if either test comes back negative, close this as a fourth disproof and say so rather than proceeding to cascade code.

findings.problem: The shot named `valley` contains no valley. The re-posed eye now stands inside the near-plant annulus and the frame is a wall of foliage with a blank backdrop. The lower right third (crop 850,820 900x350) is a bare dirt mound at roughly 3-8 m that RISES away from the camera, carrying sparse yellow grass stubble that reads as scattered toothpicks and blue-black blotches of the same lightless-card family as the hero plaza voids (1450,1050 260x90). Behind it is a solid curtain of bamboo trunks. The only clear window onto the distance (1080,230 340x140, cropped and confirmed to be background with one leaf at its edge) measures p50 217.1 / p99 228.8 / detail 2.99 — an 11-code cream gradient with no ridge, no bamboo sea, no mist banding, no water. The mid-distance bamboo at 20-40 m (1150,400 420x180) resolves as lumpy dark-green cone shapes with no culm and no leaf separation, a completely different look from the excellent near culms, so the two planes do not belong to the same forest.
findings.why: ARCHITECTURE 5 opens with 'a mountain shrine above a bamboo sea at magic hour, mist in the valley'. This is the only framing in the set that is supposed to deliver it, and it delivers a hedge. A vista shot with no vista is worse than no vista shot, because the composition promises depth in its framing and then has nothing to put there — the eye travels to the horizon and lands on a blank wash.
findings.fix: Clear the near-plant annulus and the near mound out of the sight line so the drop the terrain already contains becomes visible, and give the mid-distance bamboo a silhouette that recedes. Target: (a) at least 25% of the frame area below the horizon shows ground at > 150 m, measured as pixels whose depth exceeds 150 m — no near culm within 6 m of the eye inside the central 50% of frame width; (b) the background window 1080,230 340x140 gains structure: lumaSpread >= 45 (currently 11 measured p50-to-p99) with at least two distinguishable horizontal mist/ridge bands legible at 1:1; (c) the blue-black blotches in 1450,1050 260x90 reach p50 >= 45 (box currently p50 62.8 overall but contains the blotches; the blotch pixels themselves are the p1 27.2 tail — the check is p1 >= 40). Guard: near-culm quality must not regress — box 240,250 500x500 holds detail 3.5 +/- 1.0 and saturation 0.72 +/- 0.06, because the near bamboo is the best asset in the build and clearing the annulus must not be done by deleting it. Satisfiability check: (a) and the guard act on disjoint image regions (background vs the left foreground column), and (b) asks the background window to gain 34 codes of spread against a current 217 p50 with 38 codes of headroom to the 255 ceiling and 217 below — satisfiable in either direction, and it does not require the frame to brighten, so it does not collide with the `valley` exposure. The recorded lever from round 17 (sample(76,126) -> sample(120,126)) addresses (a) only; (b) and (c) need separate work.
findings.hypothesis: Unlabelled guesses have cost two rounds here already, so only one, and it is about (b) rather than (a): the background may be blank not because there is nothing there but because the fog is dense enough at that range to compress the whole valley into 11 codes. Test before touching placement: ray-march the built heightfield along the centre of the sight line and report the ground distance and elevation at 200, 400 and 800 m for this exact pose, then ablate the aerial-perspective term and re-measure box 1080,230. If the box gains structure with fog off, this is a fog-density problem and belongs elsewhere; if it does not, it is occlusion and it is yours.

findings.problem: The distant tree cover is a mosaic of hard-edged, axis-aligned rectangular blocks. At 1:1 in `wide` (crop 350,180 1400x460, upper left) and `torii` (crop 540,590 460x130) the forest ring resolves into flat green rectangles roughly 10-25 px on a side with straight vertical and horizontal edges, no crown form, no trunk, no canopy break — it reads as green rubble or a corrupted alpha test, not as trees. It is also colour-inverted with respect to depth: the forest band in `wide` (690,415 280x95, cropped and confirmed to contain forest only) measures saturation 0.093, while the mountain it visibly occludes (1300,280 380x120, cropped and confirmed mountain only) measures 0.131. The nearer object is 30% less saturated than the farther object behind it. Same story in `hero`: treeline at 40,350 300x90 reads saturation 0.087 / meanRGB [104.2,100.9,100.8] — achromatic grey — against the mountain slope behind it at 0.271.
findings.why: Aerial perspective running backwards is one of the few errors a viewer detects instantly without knowing why: the middle distance detaches and the whole background flattens into a matte painting. Combined with the rectangular blocking, the entire 100-400 m band — which is most of the picture in the establishing shot — stops being landscape and becomes wallpaper. Priority 5 on the list, and it poisons priority 4 above it.
findings.fix: Give the mid/far tree cover a crown silhouette and restore the depth ordering of saturation. Target: (a) in box 690,415 280x95, no straight axis-aligned edge run longer than 12 px, judged by cropping and looking at 1:1; (b) the same box reaches saturation >= 0.20, restoring the ordering against the mountain behind it at 0.131; (c) `hero` box 40,350 300x90 reaches saturation >= 0.18 against the mountain slope's 0.271, so the nearer band is no longer the more washed of the two. Guard: the mountain box 1300,280 380x120 holds saturation 0.131 +/- 0.03 and p50 159.6 +/- 6, proving the change is in the foliage and not a global chroma push; `wide` whole-frame p50 holds 90 +/- 6. Satisfiability check: the forest band occupies roughly 8% of the `wide` frame, so raising its saturation by 0.107 changes whole-frame mean saturation by 0.0086 — two orders below any frame-wide guard, and the two boxes are disjoint. Unlike round 16's failed pairings, this target is a chroma move and the guard is a luma hold, so they cannot compete for the same headroom.
findings.hypothesis: The rectangularity and the over-haze may be one thing or two. Cheapest discriminator before any work: ablate the aerial-perspective term for this material only and re-crop 690,415 at 1:1. If the blocks remain rectangular with the haze off, the silhouette and the saturation are independent problems and need two fixes; if the blocks resolve into crowns, the haze is quantising something and the silhouette fix is free.

findings.problem: The sakura canopy — the largest and most eye-catching object in the hero frame — reads as torn crepe paper. At 1:1 (crop 330,150 520x380) the canopy is built from smooth 40-90 px lobes with hard, jagged alpha-test edges and a faint dark speckle laid over them. There are no individual blossoms, no five-petal florets, no scale break between the mass and its parts, and no transition from branch to flower: the branches simply disappear into the lobes. The lobes come in two tones, a warm pink and a mauve that reads as bruising, which at distance turns the crown grey-violet (400,200 250x180, saturation 0.301). At contact-sheet size it passes; at native it is the first thing that fails.
findings.why: A blossoming sakura is the signature image of the setting and both reference titles build set pieces around it. The eye knows what cherry blossom looks like better than it knows what a shrine roof looks like, so this is the object with the least tolerance for approximation in the entire frame. Card-sized lobes on an 11 m tree put the smallest visible feature at 22-36% of the crown diameter, which is roughly two orders of magnitude too coarse.
findings.fix: Reduce the blossom card half-extent so the smallest visible lobe in `hero` crop 330,150 520x380 is <= 18 px rather than the current 40-90, and break the cluster into more, smaller, varied-yaw cards so the crown silhouette gains high-frequency edge instead of smooth lobes. Target: box 400,200 250x180 reaches detail >= 14.0 (currently 9.54; the honden roof in the same frame, a surface with genuine fine structure, measures 10.54, and blossom should exceed it) with lumaSpread held at 154.6 +/- 20 so the gain is texture and not contrast. Guard: `hero` whole-frame p50 holds 76 +/- 3 and the triangle count for the blossom clusters must be reported against the ARCHITECTURE 7 budget of 900k before and after — round 16 measured one owner's triangle estimate 21k low, so quote the level rollup and not your own arithmetic. Satisfiability check: box 400,200 250x180 is 45,000 px = 1.5% of frame and the target is a Laplacian change with the luma distribution explicitly pinned, so it cannot move whole-frame p50 at all; target and guard are mutually satisfiable. MUST LAND IN THE SAME ROUND AS FINDING 10 (the floret texture in Foliage.js) — the round-16 record states that changing card size without re-authoring the texture regresses the canopy, and either change alone will make this worse.
findings.hypothesis: None offered. The card-size figure is measured off the image, not inferred from code.

findings.problem: Every banner in the set is a rigid flat rectangle and there is no visible wind anywhere in any of the five frames. At 1:1 in `sun` (crop 940,440 400x460) the nobori is a perfect trapezoid with dead-straight edges: no fold, no curl, no hem, no flutter, no cloth thickness, and — despite being directly backlit by a low sun — no translucency at all. The dark banner beside it is the same. The same rigid cards appear in `wide` (crop 700,780 1200x390, left of the torii) and `torii`. The shide hanging from the shimenawa in `torii` are flat cream cards with a single static bend. Grass, bamboo and blossom are likewise frozen in identical postures across the set.
findings.why: ARCHITECTURE 5 non-negotiable #5 is 'wind that visibly propagates as gusts across grass, bamboo, banners and cloth', and this is not a nice-to-have — in Tsushima it is the game's entire visual signature and the thing a stranger names first when asked why it looks alive. A still frame cannot show propagation, but it must show its instantaneous evidence: cloth caught mid-curl, grass laid over in a coherent direction, blossom streaming. Here every soft object is at rest and the place reads as a diorama.
findings.fix: Banner and shide geometry must consume the wind field (WORLD contract section 10: ctx.weather.windAt / the WIND_GLSL bend functions, never a local re-implementation) and must have enough spanwise segments to fold. Target, checkable on a still: in `sun` crop 940,440 400x460 the nobori's free edge must deviate from a straight line by >= 15 px over its length, with at least two visible folds crossing the cloth, and its backlit side must show translucency — box on the cloth reaching >= 1.25x the luma of the same cloth's front-facing side. Guard: `sun` whole-frame p50 holds 111 +/- 4 and the added triangles are reported against the ARCHITECTURE 7 900k budget from the level rollup, not from an owner estimate. Satisfiability check: the two banners together cover roughly 55,000 px = 1.9% of the `sun` frame and the target is a geometry/silhouette change with a luma guard on the whole frame, so they act on different quantities and cannot compete. Do not implement gust maths in this file — import it.
findings.hypothesis: None offered. Whether the banners are unsegmented, or segmented but not subscribed to the wind uniforms, is visible only in code; both would produce this image and the owner can distinguish them in a minute.

findings.problem: The establishing shot has no true blacks and no clean highlights. The whole frame lives between code 11 and 220: p0.1 = 11, p1 = 18, p5 = 27, p50 = 90, p95 = 168, p99 = 196, p99.9 = 220. Only 0.005% of pixels exceed 240 and only 0.011% fall below 8, so 95% of the image is compressed into the 150-code band [18,168]. Nothing anchors either end — not the deep shade under the honden's raised floor, not the fifteen lantern flames, not the snowfields on the massif. Compare the two frames in the same set that do work: `torii` runs p0.1 = 0 to p99.9 = 251, `hero` runs 0 to 236.
findings.why: Priority 1 on the critic list, and it is first because a washed frame reads as amateur before the viewer consciously notices anything else. Without a black point the image has no weight and no depth cue; without a highlight it has no light source. This is the frame that would be the store image and it is the flattest in the set.
findings.fix: Restore both ends of the `wide` histogram. Target: p0.1 <= 8 and p99.9 >= 235, with p50 held at 90 +/- 8 and p5/p95 moving outward rather than the midtones moving. Guard: the two frames that already pass must not regress — `torii` holds p0.1 = 0 and pctBelow8 4.538% +/- 1.0, and `hero` holds p0.1 = 0 and pctBelow8 3.806% +/- 1.0, because the round-16 crush regression was created exactly by trading one frame's toe against another's. Satisfiability check: p0.1 <= 8 needs 2,962 pixels below code 8 and the frame currently has 326; the shade under the honden's raised floor, the fence bases and the lantern undersides supply well over that count and all currently sit at 18-40. p99.9 >= 235 needs 2,962 pixels above 235 and the frame has 148; fifteen lantern flames at roughly 200 px each supply ~3,000. Both ends are reachable from populations that exist, and both move pixels away from the median rather than through it, so the p50 guard is not stressed. MUST LAND WITH FINDING 3 — adding the missing key light to the plateau is what physically creates these blacks and highlights, and grading them in without it would produce the same number from a lie and erase the evidence for finding 3. If finding 3 lands first, re-measure before doing anything here; it may already be satisfied.
findings.hypothesis: None offered — the numbers are the finding.

findings.problem: The massif is one flat form wearing a single tiling texture, with no light direction on it. At 1:1 (crop 350,180 1400x460 in `wide`; box 1300,280 380x120, cropped and confirmed mountain only) the whole range carries the same curly streak pattern at one scale — no strata, no ridgelines running down the slopes, no couloirs, no varied rock, and no lit face against a shadow face anywhere across a 1.5 km silhouette. It measures p50 159.6 / lumaSpread 53.7 / saturation 0.131 / detail 5.22. Its base meets the plateau on a hard straight horizontal with no mist gradient. The snow peaks to the right are separate hard white triangles that do not blend into the same range.
findings.why: A mountain with no light direction cannot tell the viewer where the sun is, and a mountain with one texture at one scale reads as marbled paper. In both reference titles the far range is what makes the world feel large; here it is a backdrop and it caps the depth of every wide framing.
findings.fix: Give the massif a lit face and a shadow face and break the single-scale texture. Target: box 1300,280 380x120 (sunward slope) and a matching box on the anti-sunward slope must differ in p50 by >= 25 codes and in R/B by >= 0.20, and the sunward box reaches lumaSpread >= 75 (currently 53.7) with detail held at 5.22 +/- 1.5 — the ask is low-frequency structure, not more fine grain, and `detail` provably cannot see the former, so it is used here only as a do-no-harm guard. Add a mist gradient at the base so the mountain/plateau boundary is not a straight horizontal. Guard: `wide` whole-frame p50 holds 90 +/- 6, and the mountain's saturation holds 0.131 +/- 0.04 so the change is tonal and not a chroma push. Satisfiability check: the massif occupies roughly 22% of the `wide` frame; splitting it into a lighter and a darker face about its current p50 moves pixels symmetrically in both directions, so the frame median is preserved by construction — the +/- 6 guard has ample margin and does not fight the 25-code target.

findings.problem: The blossom texture has no florets. Even setting aside the card size in finding 6, the surface inside each lobe is a smooth two-tone pink wash carrying only a faint dark speckle: box 400,200 250x180 measures detail 9.54, below the honden roof in the same frame at 10.54, and there is no petal shape at any scale. At the ~8x minification this texture runs at in `torii`, finer detail would mip to a flatter wash still.
findings.why: Cherry blossom is the one texture in this setting a viewer can check against memory. A pink wash with speckle reads as a texture stand-in that was never finished, and it undercuts the best-composed frame in the set.
findings.fix: Re-author the blossom atlas with legible five-petal florets sized to the new card extent from finding 6, plus a mip chain that preserves petal contrast rather than averaging to flat. Target: box 400,200 250x180 reaches detail >= 14.0 measured after finding 6's card change, with lumaSpread held at 154.6 +/- 20 and saturation held at 0.301 +/- 0.04. Guard: `hero` whole-frame p50 holds 76 +/- 3; textures budget stays within the ARCHITECTURE 7 48 MB ceiling and the number is quoted from the runtime report, not estimated. Satisfiability check: the box is 1.5% of frame and the target is a Laplacian move with luma and chroma both explicitly pinned, so it cannot move the frame-wide guard — mutually satisfiable. MUST LAND IN THE SAME ROUND AS FINDING 6; the round-16 record is explicit that the card-size change and the texture re-author regress the canopy if separated, and the shared detail target above is deliberately the same number so that neither owner can claim it alone.
